title: Create a ServiceAccount and Restrict It
description: Use a dedicated ServiceAccount with a Role that only allows listing Pods.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal
Create a ServiceAccount `pod-lister`, grant it permission to only list Pods in the `default` namespace, and test the permissions.

### Steps
1. Create the ServiceAccount: `kubectl create serviceaccount pod-lister`.
2. Create a Role named `pod-lister-role` that allows `get`, `list`, `watch` on `pods` in the core API group.
   - Use a YAML file or imperative: `kubectl create role pod-lister-role --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods --dry-run=client -o yaml > role.yaml` then edit if needed.
3. Create a RoleBinding named `pod-lister-binding` that binds this Role to the ServiceAccount `pod-lister`.
   - `kubectl create rolebinding pod-lister-binding --role=pod-lister-role --serviceaccount=default:pod-lister --dry-run=client -o yaml > binding.yaml`.
4. Apply the Role and RoleBinding.
5. Test access: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:default:pod-lister`.
   It should return `yes`.
6. Test that it cannot create Pods: `kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=system:serviceaccount:default:pod-lister`. Should return `no`.
7. (Optional) Create a Pod that uses this ServiceAccount and verify its identity.
   - Pod spec: `serviceAccountName: pod-lister`.
   - Exec into the Pod (if it has curl/kubectl) and try to list Pods; but by default the default namespace SA might not have token auto‑mounted? It will be, but you can test via `cat /var/run/secrets/.../token` and using curl manually.
8. Clean up the ServiceAccount, Role, and RoleBinding.
hints: If the `kubectl auth can-i` returns `no`, check that the Role and RoleBinding are created correctly and the SA name matches.
Use `-n default` if you are not in the default namespace.
The token auto‑mount is on by default; if you set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the SA or Pod, you won't get a token.
expectedOutput: `kubectl auth can-i list pods` returns yes; `create pods` returns no.
solutionCode:
kubectl create serviceaccount pod-lister
kubectl create role pod-lister-role --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods
kubectl create rolebinding pod-lister-binding --role=pod-lister-role --serviceaccount=default:pod-lister
kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:default:pod-lister
kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=system:serviceaccount:default:pod-lister
